**EXECUTIVE SUMMARY — San Jose/SF Bay vending route (BizQuest BW2489375)**

**Verdict: PASS.**

**The listing:** $135K asking, $284K gross revenue — but SDE/cash flow, machine count, and location count are all hidden (sign-in gated). Region is SF County, not San Jose. Seller claims "$800–1,000 net/machine/month" and "~1 hr/machine/week, semi-passive."

**Three independent problems, any one disqualifying:**

1. **Immigration (fatal as framed).** TN bars Hooman from self-operating a US business — USCIS explicitly reinforced the self-employment ban in a July 2025 policy update. "Personally overseeing/restocking" is active work, not passive investment. And if his wife is a TD dependent spouse, she **cannot legally work** in the US at all — so "his wife runs it" doesn't rescue the deal. Her status is UNKNOWN and must be confirmed by an immigration lawyer before anything else. This makes "a business he/his wife personally oversees" legally unavailable today.

2. **Priced rich for the asset class.** Vending routes sell for 0.5–1.1x SDE (Regalis). At the industry-normal 25–30% net, $284K gross implies ~$71–85K SDE, so $135K is ~1.6–1.9x — roughly 40–90% over market. On TN he can't use SBA/leverage, so it's all-cash at a full price.

3. **Numbers don't reconcile + not passive.** The per-machine claim is ~2.5–3x the industry norm ($160–825/mo, typically ~$330), and it's inconsistent with the gross — signaling concentration risk or inflated figures. Real owner-hours are 8–20+/wk of Bay Area driving/restocking; a hired driver ($22–30+/hr loaded) guts the thin SDE. "Healthy vending" is a fad-prone pitch (see HUMAN Healthy Vending complaints) with no moat, in a market consolidating under Canteen/Aramark/365.

**Not even VISIT-WORTH-IT** unless an immigration attorney first confirms a compliant passive structure AND the wife's independent work authorization. A full "what to check on-site" list (tax returns, telemetry export, assignable location agreements, ride the route once, machine age/EMV, spoilage) is in the file. Better fit: remote software per the repo's own thesis.

**Summary — Richmond BC Low-Voltage Integrator: CONDITIONAL, leaning PASS**

**Live listing verified** (BizBuySell #2508428): $388,888 CAD ask / $400K revenue / $130K SDE (~3.0x) / est. 2001 / 2 FT + 24 subs / $80K inventory on top of price / 20-30% down seller VTB / Richmond BC. New detail: the Technical Lead holds an "electrical degree + MBA."

**Licensing (the good news, VERIFIED):** Hooman does NOT need a personal trade ticket. BC's Security Services Act licenses the *business* (Security Business Licence) plus individual alarm-installer workers; and Technical Safety BC's FSR (Field Safety Representative) "can act on behalf of a contractor" — i.e., can be an *employee*, not the owner. So this is the only trades deal a non-tradesperson can legally own. The flip side: those licences ride on the Technical Lead (likely FSR) — a genuine, poachable **key-man risk**, not a formality.

**"AI proposal automation" = marketing, not IP (VERIFIED):** Industry-standard platforms D-Tools and Jetbuilt (its "Jetbot" AI) already do AI proposal/BOM/scope generation off-the-shelf. Pay $0 goodwill for it; the seller takes the tool to his "AI ventures" anyway.

**Deal-killers:** (1) absentee-across-a-border on a 2-employee, sub-heavy field business — not remotely operable from the US on a TN; (2) FSR key-man; (3) **no recurring/monitoring revenue** — project-only earnings are the lowest-quality kind, so ~3x is full; (4) after replacing his own labor with a $90-120K GM, true return on ~$470K is thin. **Founder-fit is genuinely high** (EE/AI adjacency), and financing fits budget. Flip to GO only if he relocates to BC and treats it as a hands-on RMR-building roll-up platform. As a remote US-resident secondary income: PASS. Claims marked VERIFIED/ASSUMED/UNVERIFIED throughout; note that industry market-size and RMR-multiple sources were 403/CAPTCHA-blocked, so those are marked directional/ASSUMED.

**Summary — Central-Ontario Natural Deodorant DTC Brand**

The live BizBuySell listing (#2513834) is real and confirms the numbers: $349K asking, $425K revenue, $100K SDE (~3.5x, ~23.5% margin), est. 2012, 1 part-time employee, +$30K inventory, EWG-Verified, 14 SKUs, 1,000+ Amazon Subscribe & Save subs, seller financing, retirement seller. Nearly the entire price is goodwill.

**Market:** North American natural deodorant ~$690M (2025) growing ~7.8% CAGR — a durable but mid-single-digit tailwind, not a rocket. The category was CPG-consolidated in 2017 (P&G bought Native for $100M; Unilever bought Schmidt's) and is now private-labeled; a $425K micro-brand survives only in the niche long tail — no breakout path.

**Moat:** the sticky 13-yr Subscribe & Save annuity is the real asset but it lives on Amazon's platform, not the owner's. EWG Verified is a buyable $750/product badge, not a barrier.

**Ops (the crux):** the seller makes product herself, small-batch, at home in Ontario. Remote operation requires installing a co-packer (MOQ/margin hit across 14 SKUs) + 3PL + local operator — rebuilding her free labor as paid cost. Health Canada keeps the owner liable regardless. Amazon nets only ~18% contribution after ~26%+ fees plus the S&S discount.

**Financing:** CSBFP won't fund goodwill; BDC discounts it hard — so cash + seller note only.

**Hooman-fit:** low — his AI/data edge adds marginal ad/analytics value at best; diligence rigor is his only real edge.

**Verdict: PASS / low-priority fallback.** Deal-killers: (1) SDE likely drops toward ~$60–75K after co-packer/3PL/operator normalization (turning 3.5x into ~5x+); (2) Amazon concentration risk; (3) production may not transfer cleanly; (4) goodwill-heavy with thin leverage. Correctly stays #3 behind the BC SaaS and Richmond integrator.

**Summary — Ontario Cybersecurity / Security-Awareness SaaS**

Located the live listing (VERIFIED): Venturu #4008, "Profitable Cybersecurity SaaS with Gamified Training… in Ontario," brokered by Greg Kells (Sunbelt Canada). Confirmed: CA$207K revenue, 6 employees, 35+ B2B clients, founded 2019, no seller financing, remote. **Price is still gated** — it renders only "Negotiable"; I could not surface a number anywhere. It's NDA/broker-release only, so contacting Kells is the mandatory next step.

The 6-employees-on-$207K flag is CONFIRMED as serious. That's ~CA$34.5K revenue/head vs a healthy $150K+. If those are full-time Ontario salaries (~$70–110K loaded each), payroll alone is $420–660K — deeply negative, making "profitable" false and this a distressed acqui-hire. Charitable reading (part-time/contract) yields only thin positive SDE. Honest SDE bracket: roughly −$150K to +$50K, UNVERIFIED — the broker's refusal to publish any cash-flow number fits a business whose earnings don't support a price.

Market/competition (pricing VERIFIED): commoditized race-to-the-bottom. Wizer gives SAT away free; KnowBe4 runs ~$1.63–3.75/seat; Microsoft bundles it into E5. A 35-client micro-vendor has no visible moat and dangerous concentration — sub-scale roadkill unless it owns a real MSP channel or regulated niche (UNVERIFIED). Compliance (PCI/HIPAA/GDPR/PIPEDA) drives category stickiness but is satisfied by any vendor, so it protects the category, not this company's pricing.

Founder-fit: software HIGH, but sales — the whole game — is his weak spot, and for a technical buyer the product is trivially buildable, so you'd only be buying 35 churnable accounts. No seller note = all-cash, unlevered (BDC won't finance negative SDE).

**Verdict: PASS / low-priority** — pursue only as a cheap sub-six-figure asset grab after price + 3-yr financials + FT-vs-contract staffing + churn/concentration are disclosed. Deal-killers: undisclosed price/financials, full-time salaried staff, top-5 clients >50% revenue, any revenue/SDE multiple, or seller refusing a retention holdback + transition. Does not belong ahead of the #1 BC Staffing SaaS.

Wrote `/home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/acquisitions_canada/deepdive_toronto_laundromats.md`.

**Summary (~250 words)**

Both listings are live and confirmed. **6210 Finch (MLS W12836172, $724,900):** ~1,750 sq ft, 27 Electrolux washers/24 dryers (2017), pay-by-phone, "completely unattended and remotely controlled," 5+5+5 lease — but net income is only claimed ("very high"), never disclosed. **Scrubby's (realtor.ca 29874087, $345,000):** 36/36 machines, VERIFIED $6,500/wk coin (~$338K/yr), rent $7,015/mo incl TMI+HST, attended, and only ~2.5 yrs lease left.

**Economics:** laundromats sell at 3–5x SDE, but the lease sets the multiple because a laundromat is worthless the day the lease ends. Scrubby's ~2.5-yr tail is near-fatal — you'd pay a going-concern multiple for a 2.5-yr annuity, it's unfinanceable (amortization can't exceed lease term), and resale is impaired; fair value is more like 1–2x SDE. The only fix is making the purchase conditional on a new 5+5 lease before close; otherwise walk regardless of price. 6210 Finch's 15-yr lease is the opposite — financeable and resaleable.

**Diligence edge:** the water/gas-bill → wash-count → revenue reconstruction (utilities run 20–25% of revenue) is exactly Hooman's regression skillset and directly exposes inflated coin claims.

**Capex/financing:** 2017 gear is ~9 yrs old (7–10 yr life) → a $230–450K re-equip cliff at Finch; CSBFP/BDC won't finance goodwill and the lease-term rule forces both toward **mostly cash**.

**Verdicts:** 6210 Finch — conditional pursue but over budget; offer contingent on verifying processor+utility+tax records and re-pricing for equipment age. Scrubby's — PASS unless a fresh long lease is signed pre-close. One swing at most; category still ranks below Canadian SaaS. Full "what-to-verify" checklist included.
